title: Glue and align a wooden frame corner
instruction: Apply a narrow bead of wood glue from the labelled bottle along a frame rail's miter. Keep the rail fronts and bench cover clean apart from a small line of squeeze-out at the joint. Return the bottle upright to its starting area, press the two rails together into a tight, flush 90-degree corner on the covered bench, and finish holding both rails in place.
context: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics estimates 889,700 carpenter jobs in 2025. Assembling and fastening wooden components with glue is a core carpentry task listed by O*NET. This task isolates glue application and alignment of one picture- or mirror-frame corner before clamping or fastening; no cured-bond strength is claimed.
setup: Standard two-arm YAM station with parallel grippers and a 1100 x 1300 x 60 mm wood table, bare top 747.5 mm high. A removable light-blue polyethylene sheet, 1100 x 1300 x 0.2 mm, lies taped flat over the top; working surface 747.7 mm high. A white 100 x 100 mm bottle-home outline is centred at (620,-380) mm. Two loose bare poplar frame rails, each 300 mm long on the outside edge, 57 mm wide, 16 mm thick and nominally 120 g, have 45-degree cuts at both ends. The working cuts are the two ends nearest the robot initially; the far-end miters belong to later frame corners. They are plain frame blanks; backing, glazing, rebates, profiling and reinforcement are outside this corner-assembly task. Coordinates: +x away from the robot, +y to its left. Head rail working-cut centre (265,-60) mm, long-axis yaw -45 degrees; side rail working-cut centre (265,65) mm, yaw +45 degrees; both lie flat. The applicator is U.S. Plastic item 66063, a 2 oz/60 mL natural LDPE oval bottle with 18/400 natural LDPE Yorker cap and 0.762 mm round opening. It starts upright directly on the cover at (620,-380) mm with no holder, labelled WOOD GLUE; the removable red tip protector is taken off before the trial and stored outside the workspace. Body footprint 24.7142 x 50.1904 mm; uncapped height 93.6244 mm; cap height 31.75 mm. Mounted cap overlap is not published: simulation assumes 11.3744 mm overlap, giving 114 mm total height. Supplier-listed empty weight 14.515 g plus 20 mL glue gives approximately 36.56 g, lumped into a core and two 5 g compliant walls. It contains 20 mL of Titebond Original Wood Glue in simulation; physical trials use an identical prepared applicator with 15-25 mL remaining, nozzle open. Glue and props at 20-24 C. Thin replaceable clear polyethylene covers protect gripper pads; the model absorbs their negligible thickness into the native pad contact envelope. Rulers, a 0.01 g scale, square/protractor, straightedge and feeler gauges are human judging tools, kept out of the robot workspace during execution.
scoring: Evaluate at the end, using the bead visible just before the final closure when it becomes hidden. 0 for no qualifying progress; 0.25 for at least 20 mm of visible glue along either working cut; 0.5 for a bead covering at least 65 mm of cut length with width 2-8 mm, no internal dry gap over 5 mm, no pile over 2 mm high, and total bottle weight loss 0.05-0.30 g on a 0.01 g scale. Straight or zigzag is accepted; measure length along the cut, not nozzle path length. With that bead/dose, 0.75 for a 90 +/- 3 degree corner, seam gap, corner-tip mismatch and face step each at most 2 mm, with both rails flat on the cover (a 1 mm feeler does not fit under any bottom corner). Full 1.0 requires 90 +/- 2 degrees, a 0.5 mm feeler unable to enter the seam at either inner/outer corner or under a straightedge bridging the lower front face, corner-tip mismatch at most 1 mm, both rails flat as above, bottle released and standing on its base entirely inside the home outline (within 10 degrees of vertical), and each gripper closed on a distinct rail. These conditions must hold for the final 2 s with rail-corner motion at most 2 mm, measured against the bench. Either hand assignment and any effective grasp are accepted. Normal squeeze-out within 2 mm of the seated seam is allowed. More than 25 mm^2 total visible glue elsewhere on finished rail faces or the cover caps the score at 0.5; sum touched 1 mm photo-grid cells, including separate spots. The bottle falling off the bench (its base passing 50 mm below the covered top) permanently scores 0. There is no wood-drop penalty: remaining bead and final corner determine its credit. Simulation failure/nonfinite state is an invalid trial, not an invented robot score. README specifies photos, weighing, gauges and post-run inspection while the arms keep holding.
reset_notes: The robot never refills the bottle. Use the prepared Titebond Original applicator without topping up between trials while it remains within the 15-25 mL preparation band; swap in another prepared bottle when necessary. Before setup, record gross bottle weight for preparation and tare a 0.01 g scale with that bottle; retain the tare through the trial. After execution, replace the unchanged bottle and negate the displayed reading for weight loss; do not subtract independently rounded gross weights. Reset poses, use clean dry rails or a fresh matched pair, replace a soiled blue cover and disposable pad films, and wipe any wet residue with water before it dries. Native reset clears deposits and reinitializes the 20 mL reservoir; this is experiment preparation, not a robot action.
fidelity: Native rigid-body/gripper contact; no snapping or grasp/adhesive attachments. Glue is a conserved 1 mm surface raster driven by measured squeeze and nozzle placement, with approximate flow/wetting and no absorption or cure. U.S. Plastic 66063 dimensions/material are referenced; cap overlap, shoulder shape, wall compliance and constant initial mass are estimated. The fixed 0.2 mm cover omits wrinkles; nominal friction and LDPE opacity are simplified. See README for details.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 over 2,400 actions (120 s), one continuous session; scripted demo: 1.0 in 1,747 actions (87.35 s). Both use the U.S. Plastic 66063 reference bottle, covered frame scene and observable-frame-v1 rubric.
